text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The results of the investigation by the public prosecutor's office of possible violations of the anti-corruption law will be announced next week.

- The man who drew up the anti-corruption law, deputy Janis Lagzdins from government party Latvia's Way, said the dismissal of both the cabinet and parliament would be the best solution to end a series of corruption scandals as the register shows MPs and ministers breaking the law by holding official jobs and posts in private businesses.
- Parliament passed a law on private pension funds, effective from January 1, 1998.

- New facts proving disorder in the company register: according to the register, the director of the state revenue service, Andreis Sonchiks, is still serving as a chief accountant at the Priekule experiment station.
- President Suleyman Demirel said Latvia may be sure of Turkey's support for its integration into NATO.

- The anti-corruption campaign hits not only officials but also their relatives. The accounting records of the cinema Kino 52 and coffee shop Charles owned by Sarmite Pika, the wife of Culture Minister Rihards Piks, were subject to a check by the State revenue service early this week.

- A controlling stake in Riga railway car works is due to be put up for auction tomorrow. The auction was put off a month ago after the privatisation agency revealed that one of the two potential buyers, Latek, may owe money to the plant.
- Parliament passed at the first reading a new official language law, which tightens the rules for using Latvian in both the public and education spheres.
- The Radisson SAS hotel is hosting an international conference on personnel management.

- After having bought the Ogre knitting plant, the owners of the Baltijas holdings company are searching for partners among the world's leading producers of knitwear to make the plant a part of an international conglomerate.
- The privatisation agency finished formulating the rules to privatise the Liepaja match factory. The plant's tunover doubled in 1996 to 1.325 million lats.
